<!--
Reads one run's res_sim_<run>.RDS from each scenario x censoring cell
(surv_analysis.R output), not surv_all.RDS, plus surv_metrics.RDS if it is
there. From competing_risk/:
  quarto render surv_pointwise.qmd
Another run, rho or results folder:
  quarto render surv_pointwise.qmd -P run:7 -P rho:0 -P res_path:<dir>
-->

```{r setup, include=FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(echo = FALSE, warning = FALSE, message = FALSE,
                       fig.width = 11, fig.height = 9)
```

```{r libraries, include=FALSE}
library(dplyr)
library(tidyr)
library(purrr)
library(ggplot2)
library(here)
library(knitr)
source(here("competing_risk", "surv_config.R"))
source(here("R", "metrics.R"))
source(here("R", "figures.R"))
```

## What this shows

`surv_results.qmd` summarises each run by one number per metric. This report
takes a single run (run **`r params$run`**, ρ = **`r params$rho`**, n = 500) in
every scenario × censoring cell and plots each estimator's CATE unit by unit,
against the truth, across the trial population.

| Scenario | Treatment effect |
|---|---|
| 1 | ATE on E1 only |
| 2 | ATE on E2 only |
| 3 | HTE on E1, no ATE on E2 |
| 4 | HTE on E1, ATE on E2 |
| 5 | HTE on E2, no ATE on E1 |
| 6 | HTE on E2, ATE on E1 |
| 7 | HTE on both |

The treatment acts on the Weibull scales, with X3 (binary) the effect
modifier; X1 (binary) and X2 (continuous) are prognostic. The true CATE
depends on X1, X2 and X3 only, so it is plotted against X2, the one continuous
covariate, where it draws as up to four curves (X1 × X3).

**Arms.** Only each family's production fitting strategy
(`R/figures.R::SURV_ARM_LABELS`, see `README.md`, "Crossfitting"), no
semi-oracles.

**One scale.** The arms target different estimands: IPW and CSF-cs the net
(cause-specific) RMST difference, CSF-sh the subdistribution RMST difference,
the pseudo-value arms the RMTL difference. Here the three RMST arms have their
estimate *and* truth negated, so every panel reads as **time lost to the
event** (positive = treatment makes the event take more of the 28 days). CSF-sh
then targets exactly the RMTL difference; IPW and CSF-cs still target the net
version, so their black truth differs from the other rows'. Each arm is scored
against its own truth, and their bias is the negative of `surv_metrics.R`'s.

A run is seeded by its run index alone, so all 14 cells share W and the
covariates; the censoring pair and the scenarios differ in the outcome only.
The estimates are the ones the metrics score: in-sample on the trial's own
units (out-of-bag, or cross-fitted for the SuperLearner arms).

```{r data}
if (nzchar(params$res_path)) study$res_path <- params$res_path
RHO <- as.numeric(params$rho)
RUN <- as.integer(params$run)
N <- 500

ARMS <- names(SURV_ARM_LABELS)
ARM_COLOURS <- setNames(
  as.character(paletteer::paletteer_d("rcartocolor::Safe")[seq_along(ARMS)]),
  unname(SURV_ARM_LABELS)
)

# the estimate's name in sim_res[[arm]] and its truth column, per event - as
# surv_metrics.R's framework_targets / framework_truth_map, narrowed to these
# arms and to Events 1 and 2
TARGETS <- c(
  setNames(rep(list(c(`Event 1` = "RMST1", `Event 2` = "RMST2")), 3),
           c("ipw", "csf_cs", "csf_sh")),
  setNames(rep(list(c(`Event 1` = "RMTL1", `Event 2` = "RMTL2")), 5),
           setdiff(ARMS, c("ipw", "csf_cs", "csf_sh")))
)
TRUTH <- list(
  ipw    = c(RMST1 = "tau_RMST1_cs", RMST2 = "tau_RMST2_cs"),
  csf_cs = c(RMST1 = "tau_RMST1_cs", RMST2 = "tau_RMST2_cs"),
  csf_sh = c(RMST1 = "tau_RMST1",    RMST2 = "tau_RMST2")
)
for (a in setdiff(ARMS, names(TRUTH))) {
  TRUTH[[a]] <- c(RMTL1 = "tau_RMTL1", RMTL2 = "tau_RMTL2")
}
# RMST arms are negated onto the lost-time scale
SIGN <- ifelse(ARMS %in% c("ipw", "csf_cs", "csf_sh"), -1, 1)
names(SIGN) <- ARMS

# the DR arms' saved pseudo-outcomes, by nuisance path
PO_SOURCES <- list(
  pseudo_dr_whole_oob = c("rf", "whole_oob"),
  rsf_dr_oob = c("rsf", "oob"),
  sl_dr_whole = c("sl", "whole")
)

cells <- expand.grid(scenario = 1:7, censoring = c(TRUE, FALSE))
cells$file <- vapply(seq_len(nrow(cells)), function(i) {
  file.path(combo_dir(study, list(rho = RHO, scenario = cells$scenario[i], n = N,
                                  censoring = cells$censoring[i])),
            paste0("res_sim_", RUN, ".RDS"))
}, character(1))
cells$found <- file.exists(cells$file)

#' One run's per-unit estimates and DR pseudo-outcomes, in long form
read_cell <- function(scenario, censoring, file) {
  sim_res <- readRDS(file)
  d <- sim_res$data
  units <- tibble(scenario = scenario, censoring = censoring,
                  unit = seq_len(nrow(d)), W = d$W, X1 = d$X1, X2 = d$X2,
                  X3 = d$X3)

  est <- bind_rows(lapply(intersect(ARMS, names(sim_res)), function(a) {
    bind_rows(lapply(names(TARGETS[[a]]), function(ev) {
      tgt <- TARGETS[[a]][[ev]]
      tau <- sim_res[[a]][[tgt]]
      if (is.null(tau)) return(NULL)
      mutate(units, arm = a, event = ev,
             tau_hat = SIGN[[a]] * tau,
             tau_true = SIGN[[a]] * sim_res$truth[[TRUTH[[a]][[tgt]]]])
    }))
  }))

  po <- bind_rows(lapply(names(PO_SOURCES), function(a) {
    nuis <- sim_res$nuisances[[PO_SOURCES[[a]][1]]][[PO_SOURCES[[a]][2]]]
    bind_rows(lapply(names(TARGETS[[a]]), function(ev) {
      e <- TARGETS[[a]][[ev]]
      if (is.null(nuis[[e]]$po) || is.null(sim_res[[a]][[e]])) return(NULL)
      mutate(units, arm = a, event = ev, po = nuis[[e]]$po,
             tau_hat = sim_res[[a]][[e]],
             tau_true = sim_res$truth[[TRUTH[[a]][[e]]]])
    }))
  }))

  list(est = est, po = po)
}

loaded <- pmap(cells[cells$found, c("scenario", "censoring", "file")], read_cell)

label_cells <- function(df) {
  df %>%
    mutate(arm = factor(SURV_ARM_LABELS[arm], levels = unname(SURV_ARM_LABELS)),
           scenario_lab = factor(SURV_SCENARIO_LABELS[as.character(scenario)],
                                 levels = unname(SURV_SCENARIO_LABELS)),
           scenario_short = factor(SURV_SCENARIO_PLOT_LABELS[as.character(scenario)],
                                   levels = unname(SURV_SCENARIO_PLOT_LABELS)),
           cens_lab = factor(ifelse(censoring, "Censored", "Uncensored"),
                             levels = c("Censored", "Uncensored")),
           event = factor(event, levels = c("Event 1", "Event 2"))) %>%
    droplevels()
}

est <- bind_rows(map(loaded, "est")) %>%
  mutate(bias = tau_hat - tau_true) %>%
  label_cells()
po <- bind_rows(map(loaded, "po")) %>% label_cells()
```

```{r missing-cells, results="asis"}
if (!all(cells$found)) {
  miss <- cells[!cells$found, ]
  cat("**Not found, left out:** ",
      paste0("scenario ", miss$scenario, ", censoring ", miss$censoring,
             collapse = "; "),
      " (looked for `res_sim_", RUN, ".RDS` under `", study$res_path, "`).\n",
      sep = "")
}
```

```{r plot-helpers, include=FALSE}
house_style <- function() {
  list(scale_colour_manual(values = ARM_COLOURS, drop = FALSE),
       drf_theme(),
       theme(legend.position = "bottom"))
}

# event x censoring across the columns
facet_cells <- function(rows) {
  facet_grid(rows = rows, cols = vars(event, cens_lab))
}

PT_ALPHA <- 0.35
Y_LAB <- "CATE, time lost to the event (days)"
```

## This run's metrics

`R/metrics.R::cate_metrics()` on the run shown, on the lost-time scale (so the
RMST arms' bias has the opposite sign to `surv_metrics.R`'s). The correlation
is `NA` where the arm's truth is constant: the net Event 1 truth in scenarios 2
and 5, and the net Event 2 truth in scenarios 1 and 3. Where `surv_metrics.RDS`
is in the results folder, *MSE percentile* places this run's MSE among all runs
of its cell for that arm (50 = a typical run, high = a bad one).

```{r run-metrics}
run_metrics <- est %>%
  group_by(scenario, scenario_short, censoring, cens_lab, event, arm) %>%
  summarise(cate_metrics(tau_hat, tau_true, first(scenario)) %>%
              select(bias, ate_bias, rmse, mse),
            corr = suppressWarnings(cor(tau_hat, tau_true)), .groups = "drop")

metrics_file <- file.path(study$res_path, "surv_metrics.RDS")
if (file.exists(metrics_file)) {
  pctile <- readRDS(metrics_file) %>%
    filter(rho == RHO, framework %in% ARMS, target %in% c("Event 1", "Event 2")) %>%
    group_by(scenario, censoring, framework, target) %>%
    summarise(mse_pctile = if (RUN %in% run) {
      100 * mean(mse <= mse[run == RUN], na.rm = TRUE)
    } else NA_real_, .groups = "drop") %>%
    mutate(arm = factor(SURV_ARM_LABELS[framework], levels = unname(SURV_ARM_LABELS)),
           event = factor(target, levels = c("Event 1", "Event 2"))) %>%
    select(scenario, censoring, arm, event, mse_pctile)
  run_metrics <- left_join(run_metrics, pctile,
                           by = c("scenario", "censoring", "arm", "event"))
} else {
  run_metrics$mse_pctile <- NA_real_
}

run_metrics %>%
  arrange(scenario, event, censoring, rmse) %>%
  select(scenario_short, event, cens_lab, arm, bias, ate_bias, rmse, corr,
         mse_pctile) %>%
  kable(digits = 3,
        col.names = c("Scenario", "Event", "Censoring", "Arm", "Bias", "ATE bias",
                      "RMSE", "Correlation", "MSE percentile"))
```

## Estimated CATE across the population

Each arm's estimates (coloured) against X2, with its own truth in black and 0
dashed. One y scale per scenario, so the arms compare directly. The four black
curves are the X1 × X3 cells; the split between the X3 curves is the
heterogeneity, the rest is prognosis.

```{r cate-x2, results="asis", fig.height=16}
for (s in levels(est$scenario_lab)) {
  df <- filter(est, scenario_lab == s)
  cat("\n\n### ", s, "\n\n", sep = "")
  p <- ggplot(df, aes(x = X2, colour = arm)) +
    geom_hline(yintercept = 0, linetype = "dashed") +
    geom_point(aes(y = tau_hat), alpha = PT_ALPHA, size = 0.8) +
    geom_point(aes(y = tau_true), colour = "black", size = 0.4) +
    facet_cells(vars(arm)) +
    house_style() +
    theme(legend.position = "none") +
    labs(title = paste0("Estimated CATE, ", s, " (run ", RUN, ", ρ = ", RHO, ")"),
         x = "X2", y = Y_LAB)
  print(p)
}
```

## Estimated against true CATE

The dashed line is estimate = truth. A cloud flatter than the diagonal is
shrinkage towards the ATE, one shifted off it is ATE-level bias. A vertical
stripe is a constant truth (see the metrics table).

```{r cate-vs-true, results="asis", fig.height=16}
for (s in levels(est$scenario_lab)) {
  df <- filter(est, scenario_lab == s)
  cat("\n\n### ", s, "\n\n", sep = "")
  p <- ggplot(df, aes(x = tau_true, y = tau_hat, colour = arm)) +
    geom_abline(slope = 1, intercept = 0, linetype = "dashed") +
    geom_point(alpha = PT_ALPHA, size = 0.8) +
    facet_cells(vars(arm)) +
    house_style() +
    theme(legend.position = "none") +
    labs(title = paste0("Estimated vs true CATE, ", s),
         x = "True CATE", y = "Estimated CATE")
  print(p)
}
```

## Pointwise bias across the population

Unit bias (estimate − truth) with a loess smooth per arm, all arms in one panel
per cell, so where in the population each one goes wrong reads off together.

```{r bias-x2, fig.height=16}
ggplot(est, aes(x = X2, y = bias, colour = arm)) +
  geom_hline(yintercept = 0, linetype = "dashed") +
  geom_smooth(method = "loess", formula = y ~ x, se = FALSE, linewidth = 0.7) +
  facet_grid(rows = vars(scenario_short), cols = vars(event, cens_lab),
             scales = "free_y") +
  house_style() +
  labs(title = "Smoothed pointwise bias against X2", x = "X2",
       y = "Bias (estimate − truth)", colour = "Arm")
```

By the effect modifier: mean unit bias in the X3 = 0 and X3 = 1 groups. Arms
that over-smooth the heterogeneity are biased in opposite directions in the
two groups.

```{r bias-x3, fig.height=16}
est %>%
  group_by(scenario_short, event, cens_lab, arm, X3) %>%
  summarise(mean_bias = mean(bias, na.rm = TRUE), .groups = "drop") %>%
  ggplot(aes(x = factor(X3), y = mean_bias, colour = arm)) +
  geom_hline(yintercept = 0, linetype = "dashed") +
  geom_point(position = position_dodge(width = 0.6), size = 2) +
  facet_grid(rows = vars(scenario_short), cols = vars(event, cens_lab),
             scales = "free_y") +
  house_style() +
  labs(title = "Mean pointwise bias by X3", x = "X3",
       y = "Mean bias (estimate − truth)", colour = "Arm")
```

## Distribution of pointwise bias

The spread of the unit biases within the run, per arm. A box off 0 is
ATE-level bias; a tall box is unit-level error the run's mean bias hides.

```{r bias-box, fig.height=16}
ggplot(est, aes(x = cens_lab, y = bias, colour = arm)) +
  geom_hline(yintercept = 0, linetype = "dashed") +
  geom_boxplot(fill = "transparent", outlier.size = 0.4) +
  facet_grid(rows = vars(scenario_short), cols = vars(event), scales = "free_y") +
  house_style() +
  labs(title = "Unit bias within the run", x = NULL,
       y = "Bias (estimate − truth)", colour = "Arm")
```

## DR pseudo-outcomes

What each DR-learner's second stage regresses on X: its pseudo-outcome (grey),
the resulting estimate (coloured) and the RMTL truth (black). The
pseudo-outcome is built on the jackknife pseudo-values, themselves noisy and
not confined to [0, 28], so the second stage smooths a very noisy target. The
y axis is cut to the central 98% of the pseudo-outcomes.

```{r pseudo-outcomes, results="asis", fig.height=10}
for (s in levels(po$scenario_lab)) {
  df <- filter(po, scenario_lab == s)
  lims <- quantile(df$po, c(0.01, 0.99), na.rm = TRUE)
  cat("\n\n### ", s, "\n\n", sep = "")
  p <- ggplot(df, aes(x = X2)) +
    geom_hline(yintercept = 0, linetype = "dashed") +
    geom_point(aes(y = po), colour = "grey60", alpha = 0.25, size = 0.6) +
    geom_point(aes(y = tau_hat, colour = arm), size = 0.8) +
    geom_point(aes(y = tau_true), colour = "black", size = 0.4) +
    facet_cells(vars(arm)) +
    coord_cartesian(ylim = lims) +
    house_style() +
    theme(legend.position = "none") +
    labs(title = paste0("DR pseudo-outcomes and estimates, ", s),
         x = "X2", y = "Pseudo-outcome / CATE (RMTL difference)")
  print(p)
}
```
